#| include: false
import os, sys
os.environ["R_HOME"]=os.path.join(sys.prefix, "lib", "R")
%load_ext rpy2.ipython
import rpy2.robjects as ro
from great_tables import style, loc
ro.r('''
suppressMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(scales)
})

# Semantic palette. Switched 13 Aug 2026 to hex from ColorBrewer's "Paired" qualitative
# palette, per Julian's request for more distinct colors across the report. Task groups
# below draw from a separate dedicated qualitative-4 set instead, so all 9 Paired swatches
# are free for general use — 5 used here, 4 left as reserve (see below), none repeated.
# Unvalidated against this project's colorblind-separation checker (a colorblind-mode
# toggle is planned separately to cover that need, per Julian's earlier call on the
# Wes Anderson swap). Names are kept for role continuity with every figure that
# references them.
# BLUE substantive result, ORANGE failed specification,
# GREEN corrected or preferred specification, PINK flexible model, GREY context.
BLUE <- "#1f78b4"   # Paired: dark blue
ORANGE <- "#ff7f00" # Paired: dark orange
GREEN <- "#33a02c"  # Paired: dark green
PINK <- "#fb9a99"   # Paired: light red
GREY <- "#8F8D87"   # kept as an actual neutral gray — none of the 9 Paired colors are
                    # neutral, and this role needs one; not one of the new 9

# Reserve colors, not yet wired into most figures — pull from here if a new group needs its own
# color, distinct from everything above. RED is in active use (fig-diagnostics trend line).
# The first five are what's left of the 9-color Paired set after the general palette above.
RED <- "#e31a1c"       # Paired: dark red
LIGHT_BLUE <- "#a6cee3" # Paired: light blue
LIGHT_GREEN <- "#b2df8a" # Paired: light green
LIGHT_ORANGE <- "#fdbf6f" # Paired: light orange
PURPLE <- "#cab2d6"    # Paired: light purple
FOREST <- "#0B775E"    # Rushmore1
BROWN <- "#79402E"     # IsleofDogs1
MAGENTA <- "#E6A0C4"   # GrandBudapest2

# Purchasing power's own "good/bad" red-green (fig-state-afford, fig-taskchange-arrows'
# risk direction) stays on these dedicated shades, deliberately distinct from GREEN/ORANGE
# above so the two meanings never share a hue even though both are green-ish/red-ish.
PP_GOOD_GREEN <- "#1BAF7A"
PP_BAD_RED <- "#C0392B"

# Task group categorical palette. Switched 13 Aug 2026 to a dedicated ColorBrewer
# qualitative-4 set (Set2), per Julian's request — separate from the general palette
# above so the two don't have to split one 9-color set two ways. Scoped to these four
# categorical series only. Purchasing power does not get its own swatch in this family;
# its continuous maps use viridis instead (see fig-afford-map). Unvalidated against this
# project's colorblind-separation checker, same as the general palette above.
RC_TEAL <- "#66c2a5"    # Set2: teal-green (Routine Cognitive)
RM_TEAL <- "#8da0cb"    # Set2: blue-purple (Routine Manual)
NRC_ORANGE <- "#fc8d62" # Set2: orange (Non-Routine Cognitive)
NRM_ORANGE <- "#e78ac3" # Set2: pink (Non-Routine Manual)

# Task groups keep one color each wherever all four appear together.
TASK_COLORS <- c(
  "Non-Routine Cognitive" = NRC_ORANGE,
  "Non-Routine Manual" = NRM_ORANGE,
  "Routine Cognitive" = RC_TEAL,
  "Routine Manual" = RM_TEAL
)

dollar_axis <- function(v) {
  ifelse(is.na(v), "",
    ifelse(v == 0, "$0",
      sprintf("%s$%s", ifelse(v < 0, "-", ""),
              formatC(abs(v), format="d", big.mark=","))))
}

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size=9.5) +
    theme(
      panel.background=element_rect(fill="#FCFCFB", color=NA),
      plot.background=element_rect(fill="#FCFCFB", color=NA),
      panel.grid.major=element_line(color="#8F8D87", linewidth=0.3),
      panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
      plot.title=element_text(face="bold", size=10.5, color="#0B0B0B", hjust=0.5, margin=margin(b=4)),
      plot.subtitle=element_text(size=8.5, color="#52514E", margin=margin(b=8)),
      strip.background=element_blank(),
      strip.text=element_text(face="bold", size=9, color="#0B0B0B"),
      axis.line=element_line(color="#0B0B0B", linewidth=0.4),
      axis.ticks=element_blank(),
      axis.text=element_text(size=8.5, color="#0B0B0B", face="bold"),
      axis.title=element_text(size=8.5, color="#0B0B0B"),
      legend.position="bottom",
      legend.title=element_blank(),
      legend.text=element_text(size=8.5, color="#0B0B0B"),
      legend.key=element_blank(),
      plot.margin=margin(10, 14, 8, 10)
    )
)
''')

def style_table(gt):
    """Shared table typography, applied to every GT table in the report so table
    text reads clearly smaller than body prose (great_tables defaults to 16px,
    matching body text)."""
    return gt.tab_options(
        table_font_size="12.5px",
        heading_title_font_size="14px",
        heading_subtitle_font_size="12px",
        column_labels_font_size="12.5px",
        column_labels_font_weight="bold",
        source_notes_font_size="10.5px",
    ).tab_style(
        style=style.text(style="italic"),
        locations=loc.source_notes(),
    )
